evidence.requirements: Every requirement is met. tastings.js:3-5 holds the exact data, and the start page shows title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (Home.jsx:28-34, start.jpg). The links read "Book <title>" (Home.jsx:34) and the form has labelled Name/Email/Guests fields with a "Book" button (Book.jsx:90-94). The server enforces the seat limit (store.js:27-29) and errors appear next to the field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Book.jsx:65-72, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button checked against STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.jsx:57-65, index.js:5). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button that frees seats (store.js:35-45, staff.jpg). Uses React with Express, react-router, react-hook-form and zod. The UI is in English, bookings are in memory, and PORT defaults to 3000.
evidence.correctness: Seat check and insert run synchronously in one function (store.js:23-31), and a test fires 10 concurrent requests and gets exactly 4 successes (app.test.js:70-75). Guests are parsed strictly: true, '0x3', '1e0' and [2] are rejected (booking.js:10-13, booking.test.js:15). An exact-remainder booking is accepted and the next one rejected (app.test.js:60-68). Cancelling deletes the booking, so its seats come back (store.js:40-45). Minor gaps: on a fully booked tasting the form and its Book button stay active and only the server rejects the booking (Book.jsx:86-95). cancel() in Staff.jsx:42-47 does not catch network errors, which leaves an unhandled rejection. Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation.
evidence.security: The password is compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests and fails closed when it is unset (app.js:11,67-68; tested at app.test.js:125-131). The session is regenerated on login (app.js:70), and the cookie is httpOnly, SameSite=Strict and secure:'auto' with an 8-hour maxAge (app.js:37). Failed logins are rate-limited (app.js:44-51), POSTs must be JSON for CSRF hardening (app.js:28-29), and staff responses are no-store. Helmet is on, the body limit is 10kb, and the session secret is random. React escaping covers all output. No secrets are in the code.
evidence.code_quality: Small, well-separated modules: store.js, app.js, index.js and tastings.js on the server; Home, Book, Staff, api, format and useTastings on the client. One zod schema is shared between client and server (shared/booking.js). Error handling is consistent and the central error handler returns no stack traces (app.js:98-102). Naming is clear. A few lines are dense one-liners (e.g. store.js:28, app.js:93-95), but the size fits the task.
evidence.tests: Server tests use supertest to cover listing, confirmation totals, unique references, per-field errors, 9 guests, the seat limit and exact remainder, concurrency, non-numeric guests, 404/415, staff 401, wrong password, the unset-password case, logout, session expiry, rate limiting, cookie flags, grouping and cancel freeing seats (app.test.js). The UI tests run against the real in-process API (test-utils.jsx:12-24): start page content, fully booked badge, Book link to form, accessible field errors, confirmation, overbooking error, and staff sign-in/grouping/cancel/sign-out (guest.test.jsx, staff.test.jsx). Schema boundary tests are in booking.test.js.
evidence.ux_design: A wine-red and cream palette with a gold rule and serif headings makes it read as a winery's own site (start.jpg). Errors are shown as a red message under the field plus a pink background on the field (form.jpg). Success has a green heading, a note and a tidy summary card (confirmation.jpg). There is a Fully booked badge and a greyed card (styles.css:67,74). The agent's own phone screenshots show the layout adapts. Weaknesses: a plain text-only page with no imagery or description of what each tasting includes, and a fully booked tasting still opens a submittable form.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs with htmlFor/id, and errors use aria-invalid, aria-describedby and role=alert (Book.jsx:11-19, Staff.jsx:56-63). react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field (shouldFocus at Book.jsx:54). lang=en, visible focus outline (styles.css:37), time elements, and a dl for the summary. Issues: the page has no h1 (the brand is a span and pages start at h2, App.jsx:11, Home.jsx:19). Every staff button is named just "Cancel", with no booking context for screen-reader users (Staff.jsx:98). The gold focus outline on cream is low-contrast.
evidence.simplicity: Ten runtime dependencies, all standard and justified (express, session, rate-limit, helmet, react, router, react-hook-form, zod). Roughly 400 lines of app code. No needless layers. The in-memory store is a single closure.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives install/build/start/test commands and documents the environment variables, persistence and session behaviour. OpenSpec specs in openspec/specs/* record the behaviour. Strong regression tests and a committed package-lock.json. Missing: no CI pipeline, the runtime is not pinned (engines ">=22", no .nvmrc), no versioning or changelog, no ADRs, and no short guide for winery staff. The build output dist/ and the agent's .playwright-mcp files were delivered in the folder even though .gitignore excludes them.
evidence.visual_design: Typography and colour are consistent across all four screenshots: Georgia headings in wine-dark, a system sans for body text, a wine/gold/cream palette, and consistent card radius and borders. Buttons are consistent. It looks finished but restrained. The start page has large empty space below the cards (start.jpg) and there are no images or brand mark.
evidence.layout: Clear hierarchy: the header, then the page heading, then the cards (start.jpg). The form is single-column with errors placed directly under their fields (form.jpg). Staff view shows one card per tasting with the booking count in the subtitle (staff.jpg). The phone layout restacks the booking rows (styles.css:119-133, staff-phone.png). There are no overlaps or clipping. The desktop form leaves the right half of the page empty.
evidence.usability: Booking takes one click to reach the form, three fields and a Book button. Guests defaults to 1. The confirmation includes a reference and a back link. Staff see seat totals per tasting and get a Sign out button. The Staff link sits in the footer. Friction: a fully booked tasting still presents a booking form, Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation or undo, and the 'All tastings' back link sits tight against the heading.
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and on-brand for a small family winery: clean, clear prices, a dated confirmation with a reference. It lacks some warmth (no photos, no description of what each tasting includes, no address or contact information), which would make it feel more like the winery's own site.

strengths: Correct, tested core logic: the seat limit holds under concurrency, guest-count validation is strict, and cancelling frees seats, with one zod schema shared by client and server.

Careful staff security: constant-time password comparison that fails closed, session regeneration, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookies, rate limiting on sign-in, a JSON-only POST rule and no-store on staff responses.
Meaningful tests: supertest API tests plus UI tests that run against the real in-process API, covering every requirement in the brief, backed by clear OpenSpec specs.
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, a loose runtime pin (engines >=22, no .nvmrc), no versioning or changelog and no guide for winery staff. Build output and agent screenshots were also left in the delivered folder.

Fully booked and cancel flows are rough: a fully booked tasting still opens a form with an active Book button (Book.jsx:86-95), and the staff Cancel button deletes immediately with no confirmation and no handling of network errors (Staff.jsx:42-47).

Accessibility and polish gaps: no h1 on any page, every staff button is named just "Cancel" with no booking context, the focus outline has low contrast, and the visual design is restrained with no imagery or tasting descriptions.
review.verdict: This is a well-built app that meets every requirement in the brief, with correct seat handling, strong staff security and tests that cover the brief. It could go to the winery after small fixes: confirm before cancelling, lock the form on fully booked tastings, add an h1, and add CI with a pinned runtime.
